turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Thank you for seeing me. I'd like to know who decided on a zero for Owen, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.
Flattery isn't going to get you anywhere, and my time is limited. Who decided on the zero, and what is it based on?
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?
That's another family's email, and I'm not drafting it for you. I'm here about Owen, and you still haven't told me who decided on the zero or what it rests on.
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.
No. Who decided on the zero, and before or after anyone spoke to Owen?
